# From: lines that name another sender of this server, {other}, beside or in
# place of the application's own address at {domain} (review of audit stage
# 2). None may be signed with {other}'s key. Since stage 2c the check reads a
# line with OpenDKIM's own parser, so it passes those whose address OpenDKIM
# reads at {domain} - {other} in a display name, a comment or a quoted local
# part - and refuses the rest. The unit test
# (internal/milter/sender_test.go) wants every line it passes read at
# {domain}; the e2e (test/e2e/dkim_from_test.go) sends each and wants
# nothing signed for {other}. {OTHER} is {other} in capitals; {other_qp} is {other} with each
# dot escaped as a quoted pair. One Go-quoted string per line. The lines are
# composed by hand; that OpenDKIM signs none for {other} is measured, by the
# e2e on every run.
"b@{other}"
"<b@{other}>"
"\"a@{domain}\"@{other}"
"\"b@{other}\"@{domain}"
"\"x\\\" <b@{other}>\" <a@{domain}>"
"\"x\\\" <b@{other_qp}>\" <a@{domain}>"
"\"b@{other}\" <a@{domain}>"
"\"b@{OTHER}\" <a@{domain}>"
"b@{other} <a@{domain}>"
"a@{domain} (b@{other})"
"<a@{domain}> (b@{other})"
"(b@{other}) a@{domain}"
"=?utf-8?q?b=40{other}?= <a@{domain}>"
"\"x\" <b@{other}>, <a@{domain}>"
